facility_roles.quote: The Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE) is a large size (21m) Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope (IACT) installed at an altitude of 4270m above sea level at Hanle, Ladakh in northern India.

intervals.label: installation and commissioning
intervals.note: As of the January 2017 sensitivity paper the telescope was being installed; the start of construction is not given in any source fetched. The end is the start of regular observations in September 2021 (a 2024 paper calls it newly commissioned).
intervals.quote: which is presently being installed at Hanle in Ladakh, India

intervals.label: regular observations
intervals.note: Regular Crab Nebula observations since September 2021; the 2024 paper reports the first-light analysis of November 2022 to February 2023 data.
intervals.quote: has been carrying out regular observations of Crab Nebula since September 2021

name: MACE
notes: No collaboration is recorded: the sources name none. The MACE papers are written by the Astrophysical Sciences Division of the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) with the Homi Bhabha National Institute and TIFR.
No official MACE website is recorded: none was found that could be fetched.

Unresolved: the date of first light. A proceedings abstract found in a search says April 2021; the MACE paper itself says regular Crab observations since September 2021, which is what the intervals use.

physics_goals.quote: Here we report the detection of Very High Energy (VHE) gamma-ray emission from Crab Nebula above 80 GeV.
physics_goals.value: Very high energy gamma-ray astronomy from low energies (analysis threshold about 80 GeV for the first Crab analysis) with a large-aperture telescope at high altitude.

summary.plain: A 21 metre mirror telescope at Hanle in the Indian Himalayas that catches the faint flashes from gamma-ray air showers. At 4270 metres it is the highest telescope of its kind and has watched the Crab Nebula since 2021.
summary.technical: 21 m quasi-parabolic imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope (356 mirror panels, about 337 m2, 1088-PMT camera) at Hanle, Ladakh, 4270 m. Regular observations since September 2021; Crab Nebula detected above 80 GeV (arXiv:2404.01649).

unique_capabilities.quote: it stands as the only operational IACT such a high altitude
unique_capabilities.value: The highest-altitude operational imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope in the world (4270 m), which lowers the energy threshold.
